The test image shows banana fruit (pod) with progressive dark brown/black circular spots developing over 10 days after inoculation - classic postharvest rot pattern. The affected part is **fruit/pod**.

Now let me read the part index and then view reference images for the top candidates.
Pod candidates: **Anthracnose** and **Cigar_End_Rot**. I must cover 4 classes, so I'll also view 2 leaf classes. Reading one at a time as required.
Anthracnose reference shows green banana fruit with small dark circular spots - matches the early stages of the test image well. Now checking Cigar_End_Rot.

Cigar_End_Rot shows tip/end rot of banana fingers - very different from the test image's circular spots on the fruit surface. That rules out Cigar_End_Rot. Now I need 2 more class views to meet the 4-class requirement.
Cordana_Leaf_Spot shows an elliptical brown lesion on a leaf - clearly not matching the fruit disease in the test image. One more class to view.

Yellow_And_Black_Sigatoka shows dark streaks with yellow halos on leaves - completely different from the test image.

**Summary of evidence:**

- **Test image**: Banana fruit (pod) showing progressive circular dark brown/black spots that grow from small (Days 1-4) to large necrotic patches (Days 5-10). The spots develop on the fruit surface, not at the tips.
- **Anthracnose (pod)**: Green banana fruit with small dark circular spots - matches the test image pattern exactly (same spot morphology, same location on fruit surface).
- **Cigar_End_Rot (pod)**: Tip/end rot at the distal end of banana fingers - clearly different; the test image has spots in the middle of the fruit, not tip rot.
- **Cordana_Leaf_Spot** and **Yellow_And_Black_Sigatoka**: Both are leaf diseases, irrelevant to this fruit image.

The progressive dark circular spots on the fruit surface are the hallmark of banana Anthracnose (*Colletotrichum musae*), a common postharvest disease.
